newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sept forex reserves rise to US$86.678 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sept forex reserves rise to US$86.678 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves rose to US$86.678 billion at the end of September from US$86.387 billion a month earlier, the central bank said on Thursday.
The bank gave no immediate interpretation of the rise.

Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves, the world's third largest after Japan's and China's, fell in late 1995 and early 1996 as political tensions with rival China intensified into a military crisis in March, triggering heavy capital outflows.
The trend reversed after Taiwan's March 23 presidential election and a clear easing of tensions with China, rising slowly but steadily since April.
Beijing held war games and missile tests in the Taiwan strait in the run-up to the presidential poll, triggering waves of U.S. dollar buying and a run on gold.
The central bank intervened during the crisis to support the Taiwan dollar and the island's hypersensitive stock market.

Taiwan's foreign reserves peaked more than one year ago at $100.412 billion in June 1995, just as tensions with China erupted over President Lee Teng-hui's controversial private visit to the United States.
Note - Foreign currency reserves in billions of U.S. dollar.
